sense: hurt a person or an animal

terms.comment: To wound, by a blow, a weapon or a fall; the wound is vulnus (see wound). With the part hurt in the accusative: volnerātus umerum (Plin. NH 7.103, Lewis & Short).

evidence: Lewis & Short: “to hurt by striking, wound, injure, damage”
terms.comment: The general word for harm done to a body or a thing (see damage), and to feelings. For hurting oneself, mihi nocuī (see hurt yourself).

evidence: Cic. Verr. 2.1.67: Rubrius in turbā sauciātur (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Class. but rare, not in Caesar (Lewis & Short); the adjective saucius, wounded, is common.

phrases.latin: L. Cotta lēgātus in adversum ōs fundā vulnerātur
phrases.english: the legate Lucius Cotta is struck full in the face by a sling-stone

sources: Lewis & Short: vulnero · Lewis & Short: laedo · Lewis & Short: saucio
